problem_sources.text: ﻿HACK IN HILLS ’26 Problem Statements & Challenge Tracks 01. Vision-Based Autonomous Robot Problem Statement Build an autonomous robot that uses an AI-powered vision system to understand its surroundings, identify relevant objects and people, and navigate autonomously toward a given objective while detecting and avoiding obstacles. Suggested Technical Directions * Object detection * Image classification * Scene understanding * Vision-language models * Motor control * Sensors and perception * Autonomous navigation * Obstacle detection and avoidance * Real-time decision making Challenge Create a functional robotic prototype demonstrating how AI vision can be combined with robotics for autonomous perception, navigation, and decision-making in the physical world. Teams may demonstrate the system in a real or simulated environment. 02. Onchain Finance & Trading Problem Statement Build a fully onchain financial product that leverages fast blockchain settlement to create innovative and transparent trading or lending markets without relying on centralized offchain infrastructure. Possible Directions * Fully onchain order books with matching and settlement handled onchain. * Perpetual futures markets with funding rates updated every block. * Undercollateralized lending using a user’s onchain credit history to determine lending terms. * Onchain market-making systems that provide liquidity and dynamically respond to market conditions. Challenge Create a functional prototype demonstrating how blockchain-native infrastructure can enable financial products that are difficult, inefficient, or less transparent to build using traditional centralized systems. Clearly demonstrate the onchain components, transaction flow, and core financial mechanism. 03. Commodity Derivatives Intelligence Problem Statement Build a data product using India’s public commodity futures data to identify and analyze relative pricing differences between contracts representing the same underlying metal. MCX lists gold futures in multiple contract sizes, including GOLDM, GOLDTEN, GOLDGUINEA, and GOLDPETAL. Because these contracts represent the same underlying metal, their normalized prices should be closely related. The challenge is to understand, measure, and responsibly analyze the differences between them. Possible Directions Cross-Contract Relative Value * Normalize contract size, quotation base, and purity. * Identify when one contract appears unusually cheap or expensive relative to another. Term Structure & Carry Analytics * Analyze the futures curve. * Separate mechanical roll-down toward expiry from genuine changes in the curve. Walk-Forward Backtesting * Replay historical contracts day by day without look-ahead bias. * Account for transaction costs and thin-day liquidity. Trader-Facing Intelligence * Build dashboards or alerts that highlight meaningful opportunities. * Keep alerts quiet when there is no meaningful signal. * Attribute performance to the strategy rather than simply to gold-price movement. Contract Lifecycle Planning * Track listing dates, liquidity development, tender periods, and expiry. * Place every intended entry and exit inside the relevant contract calendar. Data Sources MCX Daily Bhavcopy: https://www.mcxindia.com/market-data/bhavcopy MCX Gold Contract Specifications: https://www.mcxindia.com/products/bullion/gold The daily Bhavcopy provides Symbol, Date, ExpiryDate, Open, High, Low, Close, Volume, and OpenInterest. The data is publicly available and does not require an API key. Important Data Considerations * Validate the returned Date against the requested date. MCX may return the most recent available trading day for an unrecognized, holiday, malformed, or future date. * Requests use DD/MM/YYYY, while the response Date uses MM/DD/YYYY. ExpiryDate uses a compact format such as 04SEP2026, and Symbol values may be space-padded. * Track contracts by expiry_date rather than using a continuous near-month series. A near-month series changes contracts at expiry and can create artificial price jumps. * Settlement prices are official exchange settlement values and should not automatically be treated as executable fill prices, particularly for thin contracts. * Volume is not the same as market depth or available liquidity. * GOLDTEN is available only from its 2025 listing period onward; comparisons involving GOLDTEN therefore have a shorter history. Contract Mechanics Contract Trading Unit Price Quoted Per Purity Expiry Window GOLDM 100 g 10 g 995 3rd–5th GOLDTEN 10 g 10 g 999 27th–31st GOLDGUINEA 8 g 8 g 999 27th–31st GOLDPETAL 1 g 1 g 999 27th–31st Challenge Create a functional prototype that transforms exchange settlement data into a defensible analytical signal or intelligence product and validates the approach using unseen historical data. Where a strategy or signal is presented, report performance after relevant costs using the prices of the contracts actually held, and clearly separate strategy performance from the impact of the underlying gold price. A rigorous demonstration that no persistent edge survives costs is also a valid analytical outcome. The objective is analytical rigor rather than generating a signal every day. 04. Securing Adversarial AI Safety Testing Infrastructure — Bayora Introduction AI systems are increasingly being deployed in areas where reliability, security, and safety are critical. As these systems become more capable, robust adversarial testing and safety validation infrastructure is essential. Bayora is an AI safety validation platform built around a red-team / blue-team model. The red team systematically tests language models using adversarial prompts, jailbreak sequences, and injection strategies, while the blue team develops defensive countermeasures. Together, they form a continuous adversarial testing loop intended to identify safety failures before deployment. raw.details:
HACK IN HILLS ’26, MANALI

Not a Marathon. A Mountain Sprint.

Hosted by Builder Base × Nexido × Web3 India

Hack in Hills ’26 is a 24+ hour offline hackathon in Manali, bringing together developers, designers, marketers, Web3 builders, gaming creators, and innovators to build, collaborate, and solve real-world problems with the Himalayas as the backdrop.

The team behind Hack in Hills has organized 300+ events, supported 15,000+ hackers, built communities of 50,000+ members, and worked with 50+ Web3 and gaming partners.

HIH Participants Group - https://chat.whatsapp.com/HOXOxVziXZJ6u2G85RAZog

What to Expect

  • 10,000+ registration target

  • Top 500 teams advancing from Round 1

  • Top 10 finalist teams competing in Manali

  • 35+ Web3 and Gaming partners

  • 24+ hours of building

  • Mentors, speakers, and judges

  • Networking with builders and ecosystem leaders

  • ₹1,70,000+ total prize pool

  • Offline Grand Finale in Manali, Himachal Pradesh

Hack in Hills ’26 follows a three-round journey:

Idea → Prototype & Pitch → Mountain Finale

Take your idea from a PPT to a working prototype, pitch it to the community, and earn your place at the offline Grand Finale in Manali.

Problem Statements

Explore the official Hack in Hills ’26 Problem Statements to understand the available challenge tracks, problem requirements, technical directions, datasets, resources, and evaluation objectives.

View the Complete Problem Statements:

Hack in Hills ’26 Problem Statements

Participants are encouraged to review the complete problem statements carefully before selecting a challenge and developing their solution.

Round 1: Idea & PPT Submission

10 September – 10 October 2026
Online

Submit your hackathon idea using the official PPT template provided.

Your submission should clearly cover:

  • Problem Statement

  • Proposed Solution

  • Innovation & Uniqueness

  • Target Users & Use Case

  • Technology / Tech Stack

  • Expected Impact

  • Implementation Roadmap

The Top 500 teams will be shortlisted for the next stage.

Submission Deadline: 10 October 2026, 11:59 PM IST

Round 2: Prototype Development & Social Pitch

13 October – 25 October 2026
Online

The Top 500 shortlisted teams will move into the build and pitch stage.

Phase 1: Prototype Development

13 October – 19 October 2026

Teams will develop a working prototype based on their submitted idea.

Participants are encouraged to focus on:

  • Building a functional prototype

  • Demonstrating the core solution

  • Setting up a GitHub repository

  • Showing technical feasibility

  • Preparing for the final pitch

Phase 2: Social Pitch & Outreach

20 October – 25 October 2026

Teams must complete the following:

1. LinkedIn Pitch

Create and publish a LinkedIn post presenting your hackathon idea, solution, and pitch.

Tag:

Eren, BuilderBase, Nexido, and Web3 India

2. Instagram Reel

Create an Instagram Reel explaining:

  • Why your team wants to participate

  • What you're building

  • What makes your team excited about Hack in Hills ’26

Tag:

Eren.dev, BuilderBase, Nexido, and Web3 India

3. Prototype Demo

Create a short video showcasing your working prototype and submit your GitHub repository link.

Teams must submit the links to their LinkedIn post, Instagram Reel, prototype demo, and GitHub repository through the designated submission form.

Based on the prototype, pitch, and overall submission, 10 teams will be selected for the Grand Finale in Manali.

Finalists Announced: 30 October 2026

Round 3: Grand Finale

20 – 21 November 2026
Manali, Himachal Pradesh
24+ Hours | Offline

The Top 10 finalist teams will come together in Manali for the Grand Finale.

Teams will build, refine, and present their projects with access to mentors, judges, speakers, and ecosystem leaders.

The Grand Finale will be a high-intensity 24+ hour build sprint, where teams will take their prototypes to the next level and compete for the final prizes.

Evaluation Criteria

Projects will be evaluated on:

  • Innovation

  • Technical Execution

  • Impact

  • Scalability

  • Problem-Solution Fit

  • User Experience

  • Final Presentation

Important Dates

Stage Date Mode
Registration + Round 1: Idea & PPT Submission 10 Sep – 10 Oct 2026 Online
Round 1 Shortlisting 11 – 12 Oct 2026 Online
Round 2A: Prototype Development 13 – 19 Oct 2026 Online
Round 2B: Social Pitch & Outreach 20 – 25 Oct 2026 Online
Finalists Announcement — Top 10 30 Oct 2026 Online
Round 3: Grand Finale 20 – 21 Nov 2026 Manali, Offline

Take your idea from PPT → Prototype → Pitch → Mountain Finale.

Build something real.
Build with the best.
Build in the Himalayas.

HACK IN HILLS ’26

Not a Marathon. A Mountain Sprint.
